Leaf Species Classification Report

Complete Reproducible ML Experiment

Author

Tomáš Kaválek

Published

October 14, 2026

Executive Summary

This report documents the machine learning experiments conducted on leaves.csv in strict adherence to SPEC.md. The goal is to accurately classify leaf specimens as cherry, maple, or walnut from their physical dimensions (height and width).

The selected champion model is K-Nearest Neighbors ({’clf__n_neighbors’: 7, ’clf__weights’: ‘distance’}), achieving: - Test Accuracy: 90.91% (Baseline: 42.24%) - Test Macro F1: 0.8983 (Baseline: 0.1980)

1. Exploratory Data Analysis & Anomalies

The dataset originally contains 518 rows. Key findings from Step 1 include:

  1. Exact Duplicates: 26 rows are exact duplicates of other records (5.0%). Naive random splitting would have caused data leakage between train and test sets. All duplicates were removed prior to train/test partitioning, leaving 492 unique observations.
  2. Precision Discrepancy: Rows exhibit two distinct precision levels (1–2 decimals vs. 6 decimals), consistent with synthetic jittering or mixed measurement equipment.
  3. Outliers: Two cherry leaves have widths exceeding 17 cm, placing them deep within the maple region.

2. Experimental Validation Setup

  • Deduplication: Dataset deduplicated to 492 unique observations.
  • Train/Test Partition: Stratified 80/20 holdout split (random_state=42), setting aside 99 samples for final evaluation.
  • Cross-Validation: 5-fold Stratified Cross-Validation on the 80% training set (random_state=42).
  • Primary Metric: Macro-averaged F1 score (f1_macro).

Baseline Model

A DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent") was evaluated on the 5 CV folds: - CV Macro F1: 0.1980 - CV Accuracy: 42.24%

3. Model Tuning & Comparison

A total of 53 hyperparameter configurations across 4 model families were explored via 5-fold cross-validation.

The K-Nearest Neighbors classifier proved superior, benefiting from feature scaling and distance-weighted voting which accommodates the bimodal cluster shape of maples.

4. Final Evaluation on Holdout Test Set

The champion model was refit on the full training set and evaluated strictly once on the heldout test set.

  • Holdout Test Accuracy: 90.91%
  • Holdout Test Macro F1: 0.8983

5. Conclusion & Verification

All criteria defined in SPEC.md were successfully met: - Baseline beaten by 48.67 percentage points (required: >40%). - Data leakage eliminated via pre-split deduplication. - Fully reproducible end-to-end via uv run python leaves2/train.py.
